subject: CAIQ submission: delegated proofing workflow & sample-proxy inventory
messages:
From: Sarah Tully <sarah.tully@assurancepartners.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Reed <kyle.reed@novahealth.com>, SecOps Team <secops@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ intake — delegated evidence approach and sample artifacts

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of NovaHealth's CAIQ review window, the audit team is listing a small subset of controls where they'd like to accept "delegated proofing" — i.e., we provide a canonical artifact or proxy (sample logs, configuration export, or attestation) rather than full continuous log ingestion.

Two asks to start:
1) Can you provide a short inventory of candidate proxies you can produce for control families (e.g., network controls, key management, runtime telemetry)? Prefer XLSX is fine.
2) For each proxy, please indicate whether it is a one-off artifact (sample) vs. a repeatable export and the expected TTL (days) for validity.

We have a tight window — response ideally by EOD PDT. Kyle and I can walk through if that helps.

Thanks,
Sarah

--
Sarah Tully
Senior Auditor, Assurance Partners
sarah.tully@assurancepartners.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tully <sarah.tully@assurancepartners.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, SecOps Team <secops@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — delegated evidence approach and sample artifacts

Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. Quick note: we can deliver a scoped proxy inventory and mark each item as (sample|repeatable) with TTL guidance. Marissa owns artifact curation and will attach the initial matrix. Jordan will confirm mapping to CSA control IDs where delegation is acceptable.

I'll call out where an artifact is an attestation only (legal-approved statement) versus an operational export (e.g., 7-day rotated audit log slice).

Plan:
- Marissa to attach inventory spreadsheet and README (by 11:30 PDT)
- Jordan to inline control mapping and notes (12:30 PDT)
- I will produce one-page summary for NovaHealth procurement explaining reasoning (EOD)

If you need an earlier sync I'll be available on short notice for a 20m call.

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Sarah Tully <sarah.tully@assurancepartners.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, SecOps Team <secops@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — delegated evidence approach and sample artifacts

Attaching the proxy inventory and a short README. Highlights in the sheet:
- evidence-proxy-inventory-v1.xlsx: rows grouped by CSA domain, with columns: proxy_type, example_filename, repeatable_yes_no, ttl_days, internal_owner, production_link.
- sample-artifact-proxy-readme.md: instructions for consuming the proxies and redaction guidance.

NOTE: A couple of proxies (KMS key metadata snapshots) are attestation-only for tenant isolation; we flagged them with "attestation" in the proxy_type column.

Attachment stubs: [evidence-proxy-inventory-v1.xlsx] [sample-artifact-proxy-readme.md]

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tully <sarah.tully@assurancepartners.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, SecOps Team <secops@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 12:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — delegated evidence approach and sample artifacts

Sarah, Hannah — I reviewed the inventory and added a control mapping tab in the XLSX (column: csa_control_id). Quick callouts:
- Network segmentation: we can provide a configuration export (repeatable) + a sanitized traffic sample (7-day TTL).
- Authentication/identity: user provisioning snapshots are repeatable daily; but password management proof remains an attestation.
- Monitoring/TE: runtime telemetry slices are repeatable but we recommend sampling windows (48-72h) rather than continuous streaming to the auditor for privacy.

Open question for NovaHealth: acceptance criteria for attestation documents vs. logs. Do you require notarized attestations or is a signed Redwood attestation paired with an artifact proxy sufficient?

Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kyle Reed <kyle.reed@novahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Tully <sarah.tully@assurancepartners.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — delegated evidence approach and sample artifacts

Appreciate the fast turnaround team. A couple of clarifications from NovaHealth SecOps:
- Attestations are OK if they include the signer name and a timestamp and are accompanied by at least one representative export (we expect the export to be sanitized of tenant PII).
- For any proxy marked "repeatable" we need the documented runbook or command used to generate the export in case the auditor requests re-run evidence during the audit window.
- Please add a column in the inventory: "runbook_link_or_command".

If you can include these three changes in a v1.1 upload by tomorrow morning, we can proceed to schedule the 30m walkthrough with Sarah and NovaHealth's compliance lead.

Thanks,
Kyle
SecOps Manager, NovaHealth
